chapters.title: Introduction A. Faisal Azar
blocks: In the name of God, and may blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of God, Muhammad bin Abdullah, and his two brothers, Jesus, the Word of God, and Moses, to whom God spoke, and those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

I just finished reading the book “The Annunciation” by Dr. Sami Amiri, may God protect him. It is a project that I have been waiting for a long time; Because it clarifies the Islamic vision and its evidence with strong evidence from the Hebrew and Greek languages. The book, although it did not seek to comprehend all of the good news in the Holy Bible, nevertheless established a clear argument and proof, followed up the objections with a clear response, revealed the double standards of Christians when discussing the good news, and revealed the confusion of their approach in rooting the claim of the Torah’s good news in Jesus.

The topic of good tidings is one of the topics that occupied my mind during the stage of research and consideration, before converting to Islam, especially the good tidings of Christ through Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, in the Gospel attributed to John. I have read many works by Muslim and Christian writers regarding this good news. To know the Islamic and Christian positions on it. Then God opened my heart to believe in the prophecy of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the illiterate Arab prophet who was heralded in the Torah and the Gospel.

In conclusion, I invite every seeker of truth and seeker of guidance to read the book with an open mind. Because of the importance of this topic in knowing the true religion. I also pray to God to reward Dr. Sami Ameri on behalf of Muslims with the best reward, raise his status and bless his knowledge. Glory be to my Lord, Lord of glory above what they describe, and peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

chapters.title: Introduction (author's introduction)
blocks: Praise be to God. We praise Him and seek His help and forgiveness. We seek refuge in God from the evils of ourselves and from the evils of our deeds. Whoever God guides, there is no one who leads him astray, and whoever He leads astray, there is no guide for him. As for what follows; The evidence of the final prophecy is diverse in type and numerous in number. Islamic scholars have written many works on it. Islamic scholars have also written many books exclusively discussing the matter of good news, especially in the last two centuries, after the debates expanded and their topics became more precise. As for the Jew and the Christian; They believe that their books herald great news of the future, and there is no doubt that the Muhammadan mission is one of the greatest events in history. In this book that you have in your hands, we will address the issue of the gospel, by selecting a few texts, without asking for comprehension, while reviewing the Christians’ objections and directing them to their meanings. Thus, the reader will become acquainted with the most important texts of the Gospels, and the paths of Muslims and their opponents in interpreting them in light of their meanings and contexts. His ruling on the matter will be made after considering the doctrine of the two parties.

The intention was for this research to be part of a larger book that deals with the Bible’s glad tidings of Muhammad, peace be upon him, on the one hand, and the New Testament’s claims of Jesus, peace be upon him, on the other hand, but I ended up publishing this study in two books. Due to the huge volume of research into the - alleged - good news of Jesus Christ in the Torah. I chose for this book to be brief, to the minimum of presentation, and I did not comprehend all the good news by looking at it, but rather contented myself with a selection of them, taking care to present the evidence and track down the objections.

I divided it into two chapters, the first of which is about the major initial oppositions regarding the good news of the books of the People of the Book about Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and the second is about detailing the presentation of the good news of these books about the Prophet of Islam in words, while rejecting the oppositions to them.

Perhaps the advantage of this book is that the following pages make the reader particularly interested in the Islamic-Christian dialogue. We did not organize the discussion in our book in the usual way of presenting good news. Using the biblical and evangelical texts, and just explaining their meaning to what is intended. Rather, we were concerned with explaining the questions that the Muslim will face in the introduction to the discussion on this topic, the subsequent detailed objections to the glad tidings, and how the Muslim shifts from a position of defense to a position of positive attack. By obligating a Christian to impose obligations that prevent him from remaining a Christian, if he is sincere in seeking the truth.

One of the reasons for our choosing this path of presentation, despite its difficulty for the reader who has no previous readings in Christianity or the Christian Bible, is that Christian missionaries thought that the subject of the good news of the Prophet of Islam, peace and blessings be upon him, in the Torah and the Gospel, was a weak point in Islamic discourse. To show the implications of the text of the Holy Bible for the Church on what we are asking for, and to show the Christian’s contradiction if he rejects our argument, and to point out the problems in the Holy Bible that the Christian ignores during the discussion.

In conclusion, I cannot fail to thank His Eminence Dr. Munqith Al-Saqqar for his useful comments on the draft of the book. O Lord, expand my chest for me, make my affairs easy for me, and untie the knot from my tongue. They understand what I say! Lord, forgive me for this book!

chapters.title: Chapter One: The Gospels between the original text and the seventh century copies
blocks: The Jews and Christians deny the good news of Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, in their holy books, repeating that the copies of their holy books that they have been circulating since the seventh century AD until today do not contain news of the coming Arab Prophet. This requires asking a preliminary question, before talking about the texts that we believe are glad tidings of the mission of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, which is: “Are the good news that was referred to in the Qur’anic verses contained in the original texts of the heavenly books, or are they a reference to versions of the Holy Bible that were later corrupted?” Or is it a reference to contemporary versions of the Bible for the final mission?

In order to reach what we are looking for - in answer to the previous question -; We must collect the Qur’anic verses declaring the good news of the Prophet of Islam, peace and blessings of God be upon him, in the Torah and the Gospel. To know the purpose of the references: the original text, contemporary versions of the mission, or something else? Looking at the verses of glad tidings, we can notice that they are of three types:

1. Explicit texts referring to the original text of the Torah and the Gospel as they were revealed.
  2. Texts not related to the gospel - most likely -.
  3. Texts that may be referred to the originals or subsequent copies.
First: Explicit reference to the original text of the Torah and Gospel:

In general, the verses of the Annunciation indicate an explicit reference to the original texts that were revealed to the prophets before they were later circulated among the people. This came in more than one form, including the Almighty’s saying: “And when God took a covenant with the prophets: “I have given you of the Book and wisdom; then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you, so that you may believe.” And you will surely support him. He said, “Have you affirmed, and you have taken my pledge in this?” They said, “We have affirmed.” He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you from among the people.” The Two Witnesses” [Al Imran: 81].

Ibn Katheer said: “The Almighty tells us that He took the covenant of every prophet sent by Him from Adam to Jesus, peace be upon him: No matter how much of a book and wisdom God gives one of them, and how much he reaches, then a messenger comes to him after him, to believe in him and to support him, and that whatever knowledge and prophecy he has in him does not prevent him from following those who were sent after him and supporting him.”

Another form of explicit referral is the Almighty’s saying on the tongue of Christ, peace be upon him: “And bringing good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad” [As-Saff: 6].
Second: Referring to someone other than the good news of the Awaited Prophet:

The commentators differed regarding the connection with the Almighty’s saying: “Say, ‘Have you seen: If it is from God and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel bears witness to the like of it, then believes. And you were arrogant. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. (Surat Al-Ahqaf: 10) What is clearer is that the verse is that the Qur’an is a revelation from God - Glory be to Him - and not the good news of the final Prophet.
Third: Inexplicit reference to the original text of the Torah and Gospel:

God Almighty said: “Muhammad is the Messenger of God. And those with him are hard against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You will see them kneeling down and prostrating, seeking bounty from God. And contentment. He marked them on their faces from the effect of prostration. That is their likeness in the Torah. And their likeness in the Gospel is like a plant that has put forth its shoots. So he supported him, but he took advantage of himself, and he established himself on his market, astonishing the farmers, in order to anger the disbelievers with them. And God promised forgiveness among them to those who believed and did righteous deeds. And a great reward” [Al-Fath: 29].

Referring the verse of Fath to the glad tidings of the Torah and the Gospel does not confirm or deny the confirmation of these two prophecies in the later versions of these two books after their distortion. It is permissible to say that the verse refers only to the original Torah and Gospel and is not prevented by any evidence.

And God Almighty said: “Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written among them in the Torah and the Gospel. He enjoins upon them what is right. And He forbids them from evil, and makes lawful for them the good things, and prohibits for them the evil, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. ۚ So those who believe in him and honor him and support him and follow the light that was sent down with him - those are the ones who will be successful. (Al-A’raf: 157).

Abu Al-Saud (d. 982 AH) chose the first opinion in interpreting the verse. He said: “He mentioned the Gospel before its revelation, such as mentioning what will be found in its parts, and in the end of His speech to Moses, peace be upon him, in which he was announced to him about the mission of Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and a mention of his attributes, and it was also announced to him that a book called the Gospel would be revealed.”

Therefore, Imam Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751 AH) said in a statement that the absence of the glad tidings to which the Qur’anic verses referred in copies of the era of the final prophecy or after it does not prevent it from being in the original text of what was revealed to the prophets: “If it had been decreed that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was not mentioned by his quality or description. Nor is it mentioned in the books that are in the hands of the People of the Book today. This does not necessitate that it should not be mentioned in the books that were in the hands of the People of the Book today. their predecessors at the time of his resurrection, and it was not connected in its direction to these people. Rather, those people distorted it, changed it, and concealed it. They communicated with each other and wrote down what They wanted to, and they said: This is from God. Then the scriptures became known to them and were passed down to them from their predecessors, so the changed and replaced became The well-known and correct among them is very hidden, and there is no way to know otherwise, rather it is in the absence of possibility...”

chapters.title: Chapter Three: The cessation of prophecy after Yahya

As for Christianity, there is no evidence that the world of prophecy has ended. Every reader of the Epistles of Saint Paul, the works of the Apostles, and the Book of Revelation knows this well. As for me, I am certain that Muhammad is a true prophet...”

The doctor pointed out that, as stated in the Third Evangelical Conference of the Anglicans, which was held in Canada in 1963, Canon Warren - Secretary of the Church Missionary Society - said in his research submitted to this conference: “It is possible that God spoke in that cave that is located in those hills outside Mecca...”

The texts of the New Testament do not include any statement about the end of prophecy after the ascension of Christ, peace be upon him. And Judas, Barsabbas, and Silas: “And Judas and Silas, because they also were prophets, exhorted the brethren with many words, and strengthened them” (Acts 15/32).

The problem of the early church was not the absence of prophets, but rather their abundance. This is what led her to cancel the prophecy later. The Harper's Dictionary of the Bible states: “The presence of a large number of prophets has caused major problems with false prophecy, and has made it necessary to devise tests to determine the validity of prophetic statements (Matthew 7/15-21; 24/11, 24; Mark 13/22; Acts 20/29; 2 Peter 2/1; 1 John 4/1; Revelation 2/20). Difficulties in identifying true prophets may have prompted church leaders to try to abolish prophecy altogether, and may have hastened the disappearance of prophets from the Christian community.

We do not object here by saying that prophecy subsequent to the time of Christ differs in essence from that which preceded it. The name and essence of prophecy are the same in them. It is “prophecy” in both cases, and a revelation from God to convey information and inform about the unseen. It is known that a prophet in the Bible is “(a person inspired by God who informs people of what God wants from his people, and reveals to them his will and purposes).” The prophets among the Children of Israel - previously - were not of the same rank; Among them are the great prophets, and there are those whose influence on the circle of prophecy is limited. The prophets who appeared in the first century, after the ascension of Christ, are similar to the prophets who lived among the children of Israel in an era in which there were great prophets whose voice was louder than the rest of the prophets.

As for the inference from Christ’s words: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves! By their fruits you will know them. Do they pick grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? So every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit. A good tree cannot It bears bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit. Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Then by their fruits you will recognize them.” (Matthew 7/15-20); It is not an argument to say that prophecy stopped after John the Baptist, but it is - in fact - an argument for the continuation of prophecy after Christ.

The convert to Islam, Bushra Zakhari Michael, explained this in his book: “Muhammad is the Messenger of God, this is what the Gospels announced about him,” by saying: “The Lord Christ did not say, “Beware of the prophets.” So the report is conclusive that there are no more prophets after him, then he tells us that we test the prophets by their fruits, as if there are prophets that we will know by their bad fruits and others by their good fruits. chapters.title: Chapter Four: The Awaited Prophet
blocks: It is repeated in the speeches of missionaries that no one was waiting for a prophet of the end times in the era of Christ and after. Therefore, the idea of ​​the “awaited prophet” mentioned in the Qur’anic glad tidings, quoted from the People of the Book, has no basis.

And he said, “I am not Elijah.” “Are you the prophet?” He replied: “No.”

When he denied that he was a prophet, they were astonished at his situation. As stated in the Gospel of John 6/14-15: “When the people saw the miracle that Jesus did, they said: ‘This is truly the prophet who is coming into the world!’” But when Jesus knew that they were about to come and take him by force to make him a king, he withdrew again to the mountain alone. The Jews of the first century were waiting for “the prophet coming into the world.” They knew that his greatest characteristic was that he would be, unlike all the prophets of the Children of Israel who appeared after Solomon, peace be upon him, a king with political and military authority.

Ferdinand Dixinger, head of the Department of Jewish Studies at the University of Vienna, comments on the above by saying: “We can learn from the Gospel of John (1/21, 4/25, 6/14, 7/40) that the expectation for the appearance of the “prophet” was very great (among the people at the time of Christ).”

The expectation of a prophet at the end of time is also established before the era of Christ. We know from the Qumran manuscripts that the Jews before the era of Jesus, peace be upon him, were waiting for the “teacher of uprightness,” “Madame 7,” whom they knew to be the prophet whom the good news came in the Book of Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy 18/18), and he is an eschatological prophet of the end of time, and he is not the expected Messiah.

Stephen Cook says: “There is solid evidence to show that the Qumran community itself was awaiting the return of the prophecy (1QS 9.9-11). This passage anticipates the coming of three other eschatological figures, two Messiahs and a prophet. Critics believe that these three figures are also referred to in the text (4Q175) 4QTestimonia, a document that represents a series of passages from the Bible that appear to have a blatant messianic/eschatological nature.” It does not seem that the Jewish heritage - before the first century - was stable in the matter of sealing prophecy (before the appearance of the end-time prophet); It was said that Jeremiah was the last of the prophets, and it was also said that prophecy stopped with Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi. Therefore, some of them were forced to try to reconcile these two statements. It appears from the position of the owners of the Qumran caves that there is no Jewish position that unites the Jews; Because they contradict the previous two opinions.

The critic David On drew attention to the issue of the disappearance of prophecy and its non-cessation among the Jews before Christ (according to the famous saying), and he said: “The saying that prophecy stopped in Judaism in the fifth century BC; To appear later with the rise of Christianity... But the argument directly contradicts that. Israeli prophecy did not disappear. Like all religious and social institutions, Israelite prophecy underwent a number of major or radical developments during the Second Temple Era (516 BC-AD 70). He, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said that Jesus, peace be upon him - after his descent at the end of time - would perform the ihram for Hajj or Umrah, or both: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the son of Mary will perform ihram with the freshness of spirits, whether as a Hajj or Umrah, or To discourage them.”

The prophetic news indicates that the Kaaba was the qibla for many prophets, although there is a difference of opinion among commentators regarding the number of those who performed Hajj. Ibn Taymiyyah said: “...and he performed Hajj to the ancient house that Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman had built, and he called the people to his Hajj and the prophets performed it, until Musa bin Imran performed it.” And Yunus bin Matta and others.
Is there any information in the Holy Bible about the Hajj to Mecca?

The answer is in Psalm 84/4-8: “Blessed are the people whose determination is in you. Put the ways of your house into their hearts. Passing through Wadi Al-Baqa, they make it a spring. They also cover Moreh with blessings. They go from strength to strength. They will be seen before God in Zion. O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.”
This text from the psalm talks about the most important features of the Hajj:

First: The content of Psalm 84:Christian interpretations generally agree that Psalm 84 is related to the pilgrimage to the House of God. This includes the words of critic Marvin E. Tait: “Psalm 84 expresses the pilgrim’s longing for the joy of participating in the Lord’s temples. It is a temple psalm, which can be usefully read with other psalms that expressed longing for the temple of God.” Critic Geoffrey Grogan said: “This is clearly a pilgrimage song for use on the Lord’s feasts.”

Second: The destination of pilgrims:Qur’an: The Hajj is to the Kaaba, the House of God. God Almighty said: “And to God is the obligation of the people to perform the Hajj to the House, whoever is able to make a way to it” [Al Imran: 97]. Psalm 84: “Your house” (Hebrew: הֲבֵיתֶךָ), meaning the house of God.

Third: The name of the place where the House of God is located:Qur’an: The House of God, the Kaaba, is located in Mecca, which is Mecca. God Almighty said: “Indeed, the first House established for mankind was the one in Mecca, blessed and a guidance for the worlds” [Al Imran: 96]. Psalm 84: The House of God in Habka (Hebrew: הַבָּכָא).

Fourth: The topography of the land in which the House of God is located:The Qur’an: Mecca is topographically shaped like a valley. God Almighty said: “Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley devoid of crops near Your Sacred House” [Ibrahim: 37]. Psalm 84: “Ayuk HaBaka” (Hebrew: עֵמֶק הַבָּכָא); That is, Wadi Bakkah.

Fifth: The agricultural nature of the land surrounding the House of God:القرآن: أرض الحج المباركة جدباء. قال تعالى: ﴿بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ﴾. Psalm 84: Calvin said in his interpretation of Psalm 84/6 - even though he was interpreting the text unnecessarily -: “There is no doubt that the dry and barren deserts are the purpose of this text; When they travel through these dry and barren lands, they find nothing that is necessary for life and survival.”

Sixth: The reward of whoever stays at the House of God:The Qur’an: Bakkah is a blessed land for whoever comes to it as a pilgrim. God Almighty said: “Indeed, the first House established for mankind was the one in Mecca, blessed.” Psalm 84: “Also with blessings they cover Moreh.” It is a negative translation of the Hebrew original. Mora has no meaning here; Because the text did not mention the Oak of Moreh (Genesis 12/6, Deuteronomy 11/30) or the Hill of Moreh (Judges 7/1); Therefore, modern Arabic translations have not adopted this translation.

Seventh: The spring that explodes at the House of God:Prophetic Hadith: Mecca is the place where the Well of Zamzam exploded when Hagar was there with her son Ishmael, peace be upon him. Then he gives the pilgrims water. Psalm 84: “They will make him a spring.” It is stated in the critical footnote of the New English Translation: “It says in the Masoretic Hebrew text: ‘The spring which they make.’” But this face makes no sense. Many Hebrew manuscripts... and the Septuagint... show that God is the agent.”

Eighth: Sa’ee between two mountains: Pillars of Hajj:The Qur’an: Sa’i between Mounts Safa and Marwah is one of the rituals of Hajj. God Almighty said: “Indeed, Al-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God” [Al-Baqarah: 158]. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Strive; God has decreed for you to strive.” Psalm 84: “They go from strength to strength.” The text in the Vandyke translation: “They go from strength to strength,” which is a poor translation, and the translation came in other acceptable forms: the translation of the good news: They go from mountain to mountain. Common Arabic translation: They go from mountain to mountain. This is a description that matches the quest between Safa and Marwa.
Objections:
Objection 1: The word in the Hebrew text is pronounced: “bukha”, not “bakkah”. It is in the Kha and Alif.

Answer:The letters of the Hebrew word: Ba, Kaf, and Ha. The reason for pronouncing kaf as kha here is the rule of Hebrew pronunciation that when the letter kaf is at the beginning of a word, it is pronounced kaf, and if it comes at the end of the word, it is pronounced as kha. When this letter comes here in the middle, preceded by a long alif before it, it is pronounced soft as kha. The matter is related to the rules of pronunciation, not the truth of the letters of the word, and therefore it does not change the truth of what corresponds to it in other Semitic languages, which do not follow the rule of changing the sound of the letter kaf and the rest of the letters (Bajdkaft). Like Arabic.

Objection 2: Psalm 84/6 does not mention a place called: Bakkah, but rather talks about “the valley of weeping.” This is clearly demonstrated by the most famous Arabic translation (the Vandyke translation)!

Answer:First: Arabizing the word “bika” to mean uncontrollable crying, because the verb “bika” in Hebrew has an “ha” ending, not an “alif.” Second: The most important English translations (for Protestants, Catholics, and Jews) keep the word “Baca” in Latin letters without translating it. Third: Many writers have pointed out that “bacca” in Psalm 84/6 refers to a plant called “balsam of Mecca.” It was given this name; Because if it breaks, it comes out liquid. It was stated in the Biblical Encyclopedia under the article “Balsan”: “As for the true balsam that ancient authors know, it is the “balm of Mecca,” which is still imported from the Arabian Peninsula, as was the case in ancient times.”
Objection 3: Psalm 84/6 talks about the Valley of Rephaim, which is located in an area about 3-4 miles southwest of Jerusalem.

Answer:First: Wadi Rephain, its name is apparently different from the name of Wadi Baka. Conformity requires the existence of a presumption. There is no evidence. Second: Commentator Karl Moll says that the Valley of Rephaim is unlikely to be the valley intended in Psalm 84/6 because it appears from Isaiah 17/5 that this valley is gravel and not barren as the Psalm describes it.
Objection 4: Baka is preceded by the Hebrew definite article, ha. The Hebrew definite article does not apply to proper names.

Answer:The basic principle in proper nouns is that they refrain from using the definite article, but sometimes they accept it. Examples of this include: Lebanon (Joshua 11/17), Jordan (Genesis 13/10), and Gibeah (Judges 19/14).
Conclusion:

Mecca - therefore - has the characteristics of the land mentioned in the psalm. Barren land, in which fruits appear later, and the appearance of fruits does not happen except in the presence of water. It is the spring of the Psalms, the well of Zamzam. People gather there. It is a Hajj meeting. All the descriptions mentioned in Psalm 84/4-10 agree with the command of Mecca and the pilgrimage to it. Therefore, the theologian Reverend George Bush quoted the commentator Rosenmüller as saying: “The first part of the [eighty-fourth] psalm cannot be illustrated with a better example than - and there is no question of understanding our purpose! - those who make the pilgrimage to Mecca.”

chapters.title: Chapter Five: The history of the appearance of the Messenger and his state (Daniel’s prophecies)
blocks: You have learned that the books of the People of the Book inform about the land from which the Awaited Prophet will emerge, and the attributes in it. Did the books of the Book inform about the time of his appearance? The Jews of Hijaz in the seventh century AD were waiting in their days for a prophet at the end of time, as the Qur’an says about them: “And when there came to them a book from God, confirming what was with them; and previously they were seeking victory against those They disbelieved} [Al-Baqarah: 89]?

We will use here to explain the time of the appearance of the end-time prophet from the Bible, and two texts from outside it. An indication that the birth of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, in the sixth century AD, agreed with the prophecies of the predecessors.
The first requirement: The first vision of Daniel

The prophet Daniel said: “I was seeing in my vision at night, and behold, the four winds of heaven blew upon the great sea. And four great beasts came up out of the sea, one different from that. The first is like a lion and has the wings of an eagle. And I watched until its wings spread and it was raised up from the earth, and it stood on two legs like a man, and a human heart was given to it. And behold, there was a second animal like a bear, and it was raised on one side, and in its mouth were three ribs between its teeth. So they said to it thus: Arise, eat. A lot of meat. After this I saw, and behold, another one like a leopard, having on his back the four wings of a bird. The beast had four heads, and authority was given to it. After this, I was seeing in the night visions, and behold, there was a fourth animal, enormous, strong and very strong, and it had large iron teeth. He ate, crushed, and trampled the rest with his feet. It was different from all the animals before it, and it had ten horns. I was contemplating the horns, and behold, another little horn came up among them, and three of the first horns were plucked out from before it.And behold, eyes like the eyes of man in this century, and a mouth speaking great things. I watched until the thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days sat. His clothing is white as snow, and the hair of His head is like pure wool, and His throne is a flame of fire, and His wheels are blazing fire. A river of fire flowed and came out from before him. Thousands of thousands serve him, and countless myriads stand before him. Then the judge sat down, and the scrolls were opened. I looked then for the voice of the great words which the century had spoken. I watched until the animal was killed, and its body was destroyed, and it was given to the burning of the fire. As for the rest of the living creatures, their dominion was taken away from them, but they were given a length of life for a season and a season. I saw in visions of the night, and, behold, with the clouds of heaven one like the Son of Man came and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. So to Him was given dominion, glory, and kingdom, so that all peoples, nations, and languages ​​should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and His kingdom is that which will not be destroyed” (Daniel 7/2-14).

The interpretation of this vision, as Daniel heard it, came in the same vision: “These four great living creatures are four kings who stand on the earth. But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess the kingdom forever and ever and ever... and the ten horns of This kingdom consists of ten kings who will arise, and after them another will arise, and he will be different from the first ones, and he will subjugate three kings. And he will speak words against the Most High, and he will destroy the saints of the Most High, and he will think that he will change the times and the law, and they will be delivered into his hand for a time. And times and a half. Then religion will sit and their authority will be taken away from it, so that it may perish and perish until the end. And the kingdom and dominion and the greatness of the kingdom under all heaven will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all the authorities serve and obey him” (Daniel 7:17-27).

Summary of the vision: Daniel saw four animals, each of which symbolizes a kingdom, the fourth kingdom of which has great authority on earth, in which ten kings appear, then a king appears in it who humiliates three kings. He is an infidel king, who pronounces disbelief, and seeks to change the times [two times] and the law. His authority will last for a time, times, and half a time. Then his authority will be removed from him, and his rule will be eliminated forever. A new kingdom will be established that will have the highest authority, and the authorities will submit to it until the end of time. This kingdom is headed by the “Son of Man.”
Christian interpretation:

Christians believe that the “Son of Man” in Daniel’s vision is Jesus, peace be upon him. The majority of their commentators (Hippolytus, Jerome, Cyril of Jerusalem, Theodoret...) believed that the fourth kingdom was the Roman Empire. Then they differed greatly in identifying the mouth that speaks great things, and against whom the final kingdom will be victorious. And with him comes the “Son of Man.” Some of them said that the Little Horn was the Pope of the Vatican, and it was said that he was Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and it was said that he was the Ottoman Empire, and it was said otherwise.

The big problem here is that Christian interpreters did not find any event related to ten kings and another after them that killed three kings, whose appearance could be linked to the appearance of Christ. Therefore, critic Ernst Lucas said: “There is no agreement on defining the personality of these ten kings.” Therefore, many of them tended to say that the final events related to the defeat of the Little Horn will occur after the return of Christ. It is an invalid claim. Because the text did not mention the coming of the Son of Man twice, the first time before the defeat of the Little Horn; And a second time after that, but the coming of the “Son of Man” was mentioned only once.
Islamic interpretation:

Christian interpreters generally agreed on two matters: The first matter: According to the interpretation given by the angel, one of the four beasts represents an empire: the first represents the Chaldean Empire, the second represents the Median-Persian Empire, the third symbolizes the great Greek kingdom of Alexander the Great, and the fourth symbolizes the Roman Empire.
The second thing:The ten kings who will appear will rule successively; One after the other, and not at the same time.
The Islamic interpretation starts from the previous two matters, and differs from the Christians in determining the personality of the ten centuries. To provide the answer that removes the problem:

• The ten horns represent the first ten emperors who oppressed their people. One only has to turn the pages of any history of the Church during the first three centuries, until the time of the so-called conversion of Constantine the Great to Christianity. He will find nothing but the horrors of the famous ten persecutions.
  • The small century that arose among the ten centuries, an emperor who appears after the ten persecutions. Three emperors compete with him for power. This little horn is Emperor Constantine. During his reign, the Roman Empire experienced a terrible conflict between four rivals (Constantine, Mixtius, Maximinus Daea, and Licinus). Constantine Maxentius was killed in the year 312 in the Battle of the Milevio Bridge, Licinus - during his alliance with Constantine - killed Maximinus of Daia, and Constantine killed Licinus in the year 325 AD after a dispute broke out between them.
  • This horn has a mouth that speaks great things. Constantine was skilled in logic and the ability to speak, then he declared his support for Christianity and presided over the Council of Nicaea.
  • This century is changing the times and the year. Constantine declared a decree that Sunday (the day of the sun) would be the day of rest, not Saturday, as in the law of the Torah.
  • This century declared war on the saints of God for a period of “time, times, and half a time.” The translation of this text appears in the Arabic translations: A time, two times, and half a time. Or: three and a half years. The phrase “time, times, and half a time” is usually used in ancient custom to mean three and a half times. A number of them chose to interpret one time as equal to one year. The commentators have differed regarding the meaning of “time” here. It originally means “a period of time” without specification. After centuries and a half from the time of Constantine's rule (325 AD + 350 years = 675 AD), the largest Islamic conquests began during the Umayyad era in Europe, Asia, and Africa.
The second requirement: The second vision of Daniel (the fourth and fifth kingdoms)

God Almighty inspired King Bukhtenzare with a dream in which he revealed to him the countries and kingdoms that would follow his kingdom, and the fate of every state and kingdom until a state came into existence whose kingship and authority would last forever. Daniel, peace be upon him, explained it by saying:

“As for the fourth kingdom, there will be a fourth kingdom on earth, different from all the other kingdoms, which will devour the whole earth and trample it under foot.” And you will crush them... And in the days of these kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and its kingdom will not be left to other people. And all these kingdoms will be destroyed, and they will remain forever. For you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and it broke in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold. God Almighty has made known to the king what will come after this. The dream is true and its interpretation is certain” (Daniel 2:40-45).

The summary of this prophecy is that four kingdoms will arise, and during the rule of the fourth kingdom a new kingdom will appear that will crush the rest of the kingdoms and remain forever. The Islamic interpretation says: The fourth kingdom is the Roman. During her rule, the Kingdom of Islam appeared, which crushed the Romans and remained forever. Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah responds to the Christians’ claim that the fifth kingdom is the kingdom of Christ by saying: “This is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, not a description of Christ; He is the one who sent a strong law and defeated all the kings and nations of the earth. Until the earth was filled with him and his nation in the east and west of the earth.”
The third and fourth requirements: Dates of birth of the new owner of the kingdom (from unofficial books)

The book “The Ascension of Moses” (sixth century AD) indicates that the period between the death of Moses and the appearance of the new owner of the kingdom is 1750 years. If we calculate from the year 1214 BC (the date of the Exodus) to 536 AD, we find that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was born in the year 571 AD (according to the narration of Ibn Ishaq). The Book of “The Revelation of Abraham” also indicates that after 12 hours (i.e. 1200 years) of the Babylonian captivity (586 BC), a Gentile man will appear and the people will gather around him. This corresponds to the mission of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his control over the Arabian Peninsula.

chapters.title: Chapter Six: The Paracleteus awaited by John
blocks: The good news came in the Gospel of John with the appearance of Pracletus παράκλητος. Muslims and Christians have disputed the definition of this paraclete for a long time. What is his experience in the Gospel of John? What is the truth about this preacher?
Biblical texts:

It says in John 14/15-17: “If you love me, keep my commandments; and I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter [παράκλητος] to abide With you forever is the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see it nor know it, but you know it. For he abides with you and will be in you.”

And it says in John 14/26: “But the Comforter [παράκλητος], the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance.” What I told you.”
And it says in John 15/26: “And when the Comforter [παράκλητος] comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, He is my witness.”

And it came in John 7/16-15: “But I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away the Comforter will not come to you.” [παράκλητος], but if I go, I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: and of sin, because they believe not in me. But in righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you will not see me again. And as for judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he will not speak on his own authority, but whatever he hears he will speak, And he will tell you things to come. He will glorify me, because he will take what is mine and declare it to you. All that the Father has are mine. For this reason I said, ‘He will take what is mine and declare it to you.’”

The majority of Christians have settled on saying that the Paracletus in the Gospel of John is the Holy Spirit, while the majority of Islamic scholars are of the view that the Paracletus is the Prophet of Islam whom Christ preached about in the Almighty’s saying: “And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, ‘O children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming Because of the Torah before me, and bringing good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad” [As-Saff: 6].
The first requirement: Problems of Christian interpretation

Most Christians believe that the Paraclete that Christ preached about is the Holy Spirit, the third divine hypostasis. Their main argument is the text of John 14/26: “But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things.” The text - as they say - is clear in defining the Paracleteus as the Holy Spirit.. Is this guidance convincing?
1. Paracletus...and evangelical employment:

The phrase “Praclitus” is known in the literature prior to the Gospel of John, and it has a semantic load far from the canonical understanding of the texts of the Gospel of John. The word Prakletos does not mean “comforter” as is common in the writings of Arab Christians and a group of Western researchers, and it did not appear in this sense in the contexts of its use in the New Testament. Rather, it means one who is called upon for help. That is, defending or condemning others, as appears in Greek writings since the century BC. This is the meaning in Jewish literature.

Therefore, Father Matta Al-Miskeen said: “(According to the concept of the ancient Greek language and its uses, as mentioned in the exegetical texts) we find the meaning limited to the judicial capacity of the person who practices the law, such as defense, advocacy, and intercession on behalf of others, and it was mentioned in the terminology of the Jewish rabbis with this meaning.” This prompted the critic Johannes to say explicitly: “The use of the term Pracletus in the New Testament... does not leave any consistent impression and does not fit smoothly with the history of the word....” The word has an ancient use in the previous Greek heritage, and it does not fit with this word in the context of Christ’s talk about the Holy Spirit.
2. The attributes of the Holy Spirit do not apply to the Paracleteus:

Christians today believe that the Holy Spirit is the Paraclete, but it descended on the disciples fifty days after Christ’s resurrection from the dead. They spoke in many languages ​​that they did not know (Acts 2), and this is corrupt in one way or another:

• The Holy Spirit, according to Christians, is a god. He is the third of the divine persons, and he was not absent from Christ. It was revealed to him when John the Baptist baptized him in the Jordan River (Matthew 3/16, Mark 1/10). Therefore, it is not correct to say that he is the absent and awaited one.
  • The connection of the Holy Spirit with believers among Christians and Jews was not dependent on the going of Christ; The Holy Spirit was among believers before and during the time of Christ. He was previously with the children of Israel, and was with his mother Mary (Luke 1/35). It was revealed to the disciples before the day of Pentecost, as mentioned in the Gospel of John 20/22: “And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, ‘Receive the Holy Spirit.’”
  • The Holy Spirit did not come to comfort the disciples or the apostles or to advocate on their behalf. The disciples and their followers fell under the lash of torment at the hands of the Roman authority on the one hand and the Jews on the other, without special help from the Holy Spirit.
  • The Holy Spirit did not guide the Christians and did not illuminate for them the path to knowing God - Glory be to Him -; Indeed, severe disagreement arose among the followers, and many doctrinal sects emerged, each claiming to be on the path of Christ, and claiming that those who oppose him are misguided heretics.
  • Christ's saying that this one is coming to rebuke the world does not apply to the Holy Spirit.
  • Christ mentioned that the disciples could not bear to receive many religious truths in those days: “I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now” (John 16:12-13). How did the disciples possess this ability only ten days after Christ was taken up?!
The second requirement: The Paracletus is Ahmed

Most Islamic scholars agreed that the Paracleteus is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, but they differed on how to direct this from a linguistic standpoint. Most of the later scholars said that the Greek word had been subjected to a simple corruption, and its meaning was changed from “Ahmed” to “intercessor” or “lawyer.” One of the most prominent late commentators argued that there was no need to assume that the word “Prakletos” was corrupted. The good news of Christ as “Ahmed” is not good news of a prophet named Ahmed, but rather it is good news of the one who described him as praiseworthy.
1. Pericletus = Ahmed:

Many later Muslim writers argue that Pracletus's word παράκλητος is slightly distorted in its sound; Its first Greek origin, which was said by Christ, or which was translated from the Galilean Aramaic that Christ spoke, is: Pericletos περικλυτος. This word means: “Ahmed,” which means praise and praise.

Imam Al-Shawkani said: “Ahmad is the name of our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it is a knowledge transferred from the adjective, and it may be an exaggeration on the part of the subject; So its meaning is that he is more praising God than anyone else, or from the effect; Its meaning is that he is praised for his good qualities, more than he praises anything else. Anyone who looks at the word Prakletos παράκλητος found in the manuscripts of the Gospel of John will realize that if this word were to change some of its sounds slightly, it would become in the sense of Ahmad περικλυτος [Pericletos]. Many Christians and missionaries have acknowledged this.
2. Correction of the noun:

Christians object to the claim that the vowels of the word Prakletius have been corrected. By saying that it is a claim that is contradicted by all the manuscripts of the Gospel of John that we possess; Because they do not all bear witness to the form of the Word as Muslims claim. The answer to this has two aspects:

• Delayed written heritage:The Gospel of John was written at the end of the first century or the beginning of the second. It seems that it is a transfer of a late Christian heritage, and therefore the Johannine heritage received this name incorrectly in its syntactic form. Possible, and there is no denying it; For two reasons: the first is the strangeness of the name “Ahmed” in first-century literature; The second is the popularity of the word parakletos, meaning lawyer. So the tradition deviated from the first meaning to the second, invisibly and quickly, especially since Christ’s speech about Pericletos may have been in Aramaic (according to the majority of critics). When the translation occurred, the listeners became confused with the unfamiliar name of Ahmed and the famous word “lawyer/al-Shafi’”.
  • The legitimacy of conjectural emendation:The critical community in textual criticism agrees to accept intuitive conjecture as they seek to recover the original or earliest text of the document they study. Scholars expand on this greatly when studying the Old Testament, and sometimes accept it when studying the New Testament. The reality of the intuitive guess is to restore what was omitted from speech from all available manuscripts, omit what was added in all manuscripts, or correct what was changed in all manuscripts. That is, the original text is not found in all available manuscripts.
The third requirement: The praiseworthy Paracletus (interpretation of Ibn Ashour)

The scholar and commentator Ibn Ashour believed that the word “Ahmad” in the Almighty’s saying: “And bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad” is not a proper name, and he mentioned this in detail in his interpretation of “Liberation and Enlightenment.” The summary of his words is that the word “Ahmed” applies to all the meanings that the sentence carries: the noun, the adjective, and knowledge. The Prophet who was brought good tidings, peace and blessings of God be upon him, deserves to be praised more eloquently. The well-known orientalist Montgomery Watt adhered to the same meaning, in an article entitled: “His name is Ahmed,” where he explained that the name “Ahmed” was not common before the mission, and that Muslims named it after the mission.

According to this doctrine, it is sufficient to look at the characteristics of Parakletos to know his reality. By looking at the texts; We find that the share of the Prophet of Islam, peace and blessings of God be upon him, in terms of the name “Intercessor/Advocate” and the attributes of the Paracleteus, is broader than the share of the Holy Spirit:

• Intercession and defense of others:The function of prophets, not hypostases. The Jews called Moses, peace be upon him, the word “Farqalit.”
  • Christ's saying:“I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now” (John 16:12-13). This text indicates that some of the message of revelation has not yet come to be presented to people so that they can understand it, or that the nations have not been prepared to adhere to it, even if it is understood.
  • He described the disciples as having a lack of understanding:The Gospels describe the Apostles as having little or no understanding (Matthew 8/26, 14/31, 16/8, Luke 8/25-26, Matthew 15/15-16). We commit the Christians to these texts - which we do not believe to be true - that the disciples are not the ones who will receive the message days after Christ is taken away!
  • “But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth” (John 16:13):What is the truth that the Holy Spirit guided the apostles to?
